label: Formal shirt
compositing: Draw mannequin first. Then add the recoloured regions together (canvas lighter on a transparent offscreen canvas) and draw the result over it. Do not draw regions one after another with source-over.

scale.assumption: flat chest 52 cm (size M) measured at canvas row 650 -- NOT confirmed by a size tag in this image, lower confidence than the crew tee

units.zoneCoordinates: centre x/y and w/h in canvas px, rotation in degrees clockwise
units.scaleX: horizontal squeeze applied to the logo

notes: Rebuilt from a third source photo (image-removebg-preview_2_.png) at the user's request -- the first formal-shirt photo again, but smaller (896x1114, exactly half-scale) and without the rainbow glitch artifact. This REPLACES the black-background (825x1024) build, not a patch on it.
Single colour region: body, sleeves, collar and cuffs are all one mask (mask-body.png).
_ref-mask-sleeve.png, _ref-mask-collar.png, _ref-mask-cuff.png are kept for reference only (logo zone placement), not shipped as colour regions.

Built by reusing the geometry already traced on the full-size version of this same photo (neck boundary, collar polygon, sleeve/cuff bands, the two fold-crease softening patches) scaled by exactly 0.5, rather than re-tracing from scratch -- confirmed the two images are the same pose at exactly half resolution before doing this.

Checked at full resolution on white, navy, sky blue, black and red: no neck/collar smudge, no sleeve artifact (this source has no glitch to begin with), clean cuffs, clean canvas corners, and the two fold-crease patches (same locations, scaled) still read as soft natural shading rather than a hard line.

Source image is smaller than the 1792x2228 original it was derived from -- upscaled about 1.5x onto the canvas (less than the black-background build's 1.3x headroom was relative to ITS source, so check sharpness at large preview sizes).
No size tag visible, so the 52cm/size-M scale assumption is unconfirmed.
Chest and sleeve zones passed the placement checks without needing a manual nudge around the pocket this time (different px/cm scale shifted them clear on their own) -- verify visually anyway.
